claim_formal: ¬∃ algorithm A ∀ n ∀ f∈ℤ[X1..Xn]: A(f)=1 ↔ ∃ x∈ℚ^n f(x)=0 (H10 over ℚ is undecidable)

quote_A.text: There is no algorithm which, given a polynomial $f\in\Z[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, with $n$ part of the input, decides whether $f$ has a zero in $\Q^n$.

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Hilbert's tenth problem over the rational numbers

notes: Prefix 'none': closed statement about the named decision problem H10/ℚ (could also be read ∀∃ over algorithms/instances). Family also bundles an unrelated pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational 2-torsion (Oct-7 manuscript).

claim_formal: ∀ number field K ∀ abelian variety A/K ∀ irreducible X⊆A_K̄: #{maximal atypical subvarieties of X in ⟨X⟩_sp} < ∞

quote_A.text: there are only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties of $X$ in $S=\langle X\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}$

quote_B.text: We prove the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over $`\overline{\mathbb Q}`$.

notes: Restriction is to Q̄ (number fields), conjecture usually stated over ℂ; O1 also defensible if 'abelian ZP over Q̄' is taken as the posed problem. Bundles curve case of ZP in A_2 (Hodge-generic curves over Q̄; E×CM, QM, E² branches, with full curve case combining three manuscripts) and a finite-rank Pink 5.2 corollary. Finiteness without any effective bound.

claim_formal: ∀ D∈ℝ: ¬∃ injective z:ℕ→Gaussian primes with |z(t+1)−z(t)|≤D (stronger: ∀D ∃B_D ∀ component C of G_D: |C|≤B_D)

quote_A.text: We prove the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have bounded steps.

quote_B.text: This proves the uniform form of the Gaussian moat conjecture and answers the infinite-walk question negatively.

notes: Title leads with the uniform form (∀D ∃B_D, components bounded, B_D nonexplicit/ineffective) which would be ∀∃ M8; abstract/summary lead with the moat conjecture (∀, M4). Lean fullMain covers both. Posed as a question ('does some G_D contain an infinite path') but summary calls it a conjecture; answer 'no' = conjecture affirmed.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected projective complex surface S with p_g(S)=0: alb_S: CH_0(S)^0 → Alb(S)(ℂ) is an isomorphism (integral coefficients)

quote_A.text: the Albanese homomorphism \[ \operatorname{alb}_S:\CH_0(S)^0\longrightarrow\Alb(S)(\mathbb C) \] is an isomorphism of abelian groups

quote_B.text: We prove Bloch's conjecture for smooth connected projective complex surfaces with $`p_g=0`$

notes: Matrix M7 (isomorphism) vs M1 (property 'alb is injective') is the main ambiguity. New content is p_g=q=0 (deg: CH_0 ≅ ℤ); non-general-type cases from Bloch–Kas–Lieberman. Motivic corollaries (Kimura finite-dimensionality, pure Tate motives).

quote_A.text: The explicitly defined class \(Y\in \Salg_{g,n}^{2D_*}\) of Definition~\ref{def:candidate} satisfies \[ q_{g,n}(Y)=0,\qquad Y\notin\Pspan_{g,n}. \]

quote_B.text: We disprove the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of Pixton's completeness conjecture for his original relation system.

notes: Explicit witness, prefix still ∃ per tie-break 1. Refutes for the original relation system only; no corrected statement offered (so O2 not O3).

claim_formal: ∀ d ∀ ε∈ℚ_{>0} ∃ N(d,ε) ∀ ε-lc Fano contraction f:X→Z (dim X=d, char 0, alg. closed) ∀ closed z∈Z ∃ B, U∋z: (X,B) klt over U ∧ N(K_X+B)|_{f^{-1}U} ~ 0

quote_A.text: there is a positive integer $N=N(d,\epsilon)$ with the following property

quote_B.text: This proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov's bounded-klt-complement conjecture.

notes: Matrix could be read M8 (uniform bound on complement index); chose M2 (existence of bounded-index klt complement). Outcome O5 because only the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov's conjecture is proved; O1 defensible if that form (Chen Conj. 1.1) is taken as the posed problem. Second manuscript proves the Birkar–Shokurov Cartier-divisor conjecture (uniform lct of pulled-back Cartier divisors, constant non-effective). Lean comparator is a compactness lemma about closed-chart field retractions (intermediate).

quote_A.text: \norm{Uf}_{L^3(\R^3\times[1,2])} \le C_\eps\norm{J^\eps f}_{L^3(\R^3)}

quote_B.text: This resolves Sogge's Euclidean local smoothing conjecture in dimension three.

notes: Sogge's conjecture is posed in all dimensions; settling d=3 → O5+restricted_range per tie-break 6. Critical L^3 estimate with ε-loss (lossless ε=0 not addressed). M8 vs M1: an L^p estimate with Sobolev loss; conjectured range is sharp but sharpness is not part of the theorem. Corollaries: wave maximal, Bochner–Riesz.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥1 ∀ origin-symmetric convex bodies K,L⊂ℝ^n ∀ λ∈[0,1]: |W[h_K^{1−λ}h_L^λ]| ≥ |K|^{1−λ}|L|^λ

quote_A.text: \left|\mathcal W[h_K^{1-\lambda}h_L^\lambda]\right| \ge |K|^{1-\lambda}|L|^\lambda.

quote_B.text: We prove the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension.

notes: Corollaries: symmetric L_p Brunn–Minkowski for 0<p<1; via Saroglou's transfer, log-BM for even log-concave measures and the B-conjecture (those use prior results). Stancu announced the inequality earlier but details were deferred; not treated as an earlier proof.

claim_formal: L = RL ∧ RL = BPL

quote_A.text: \[ \Lclass=\RL=\BPL. \]

quote_B.text: We prove $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$, resolving the derandomization problem for polynomial-time randomized logarithmic space.

notes: B.problem P1 (widely conjectured L=BPL) vs P2 (paper calls it 'the derandomization problem'). Also an explicit compiler / acceptance-probability approximation theorem.

claim_formal: ∃ randomized algorithm A ∃ polynomial p ∀ m,n ∀ margins r,c (Σr=Σc): A outputs an exactly uniform X∈Ω(r,c), halting a.s. with expected bit time ≤ p(m,n,log N) (and a bounded-time 2^{-k}-TV sampler)

quote_A.text: An algorithm outputs an exactly uniform table in $\Omega(r,c)$, terminates almost surely, and has expected running time polynomial in $m,n,\log(N+1)$.

quote_B.text: No positivity, balance, sparsity, or fixed-dimension assumption is required.

notes: Prior work covered fixed row count, dense/sparse regimes, or was conditional (DeSalvo–Zhao). Problem is a long-standing open question rather than a named conjecture. Second manuscript: FPRAS for cell-bounded tables (Lean covers bounded sampling, exact sampling and counting). 'effective' because the algorithms/polynomials are explicit though large.

claim_formal: ∃ deterministic poly-time algorithm A ∀ finite string family S: A(S) is a common superstring ∧ |A(S)| ≤ 2·OPT(S)

quote_A.text: There is a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the total encoded input size, that on every finite collection $\mathcal S$ of explicitly represented ordinary strings outputs a common superstring $T$ satisfying \[ \len{T}\le 2\OPT(\mathcal S). \]

quote_B.text: \Cref{thm:main} answers affirmatively the question of whether a polynomial-time factor-$2$ approximation exists.

notes: Alternative reading: P4/O7 (improving the approximation-ratio record 7/3 → 2 without determining the optimal ratio). Does not settle the Greedy conjecture (Tarhio–Ukkonen) for the Greedy procedure.

claim_formal: ∀ A>0 ∃ c_A>0 ∀^∞ d ∀ M≤Ad² ∀ ε∈(0,1/10] ∀ one-pass M-bit learner with success prob ≥2/3 on uniform signal: T ≥ c_A d log(1/ε)

quote_A.text: then its prescribed horizon satisfies \[ T\ge c_A\,d\log(1/\epsilon). \]

quote_B.text: a one-pass learner with $`Ad^2`$ persistent bits needs $`\Omega_A(d\log(1/\epsilon))`$ noiseless Gaussian samples

notes: No explicitly posed problem found in inputs; closest predecessor is Sharan–Sidford–Valiant's Ω(d log log 1/ε) bound with noise, which this strengthens (O8), though P4/O7 or P4/O1 are defensible if d log(1/ε) is tight. Family has 8 manuscripts giving alternative proofs of the o(d²) case (one with explicit constant 2^{-16}). Lean main = SubquadraticMemory ∧ FixedQuadraticMemory.

claim_formal: ∃ ergodic invertible (X,μ,T) on standard nonatomic space: h_μ(T)=0 ∧ ¬∃ smooth positive-volume model (M compact, ν smooth positive density, S C^∞ diffeo, measurable conjugacy)

quote_A.text: There exists an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation $(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space such that $h_\mu(T)=0$ and $(X,\mu,T)$ is not measurably conjugate

quote_B.text: The question addressed here is whether this entropy restriction suffices when the invariant measure must be a smooth positive density.

notes: Answers the smooth-realization question (finite entropy sufficient?) negatively for smooth positive-density models; does not cover models with measure merely equivalent to volume. Lean asserts finite KS entropy rather than zero entropy, hence weaker than the headline.

quote_A.text: For every integer \(n\ge3\), \[ \crn(K_n)=Z(n)

quote_B.text: We prove the Harary–Hill conjecture

notes: Bundles the Zarankiewicz conjecture cr(K_{m,n}) = ⌊m/2⌋⌊(m−1)/2⌋⌊n/2⌋⌊(n−1)/2⌋ (Turán's brickyard problem), also with a Lean comparator.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3 ∃ D<∞, ε>0, finite connected pure d-complexes X_m with |X_m(0)|→∞: max vertex top-degree ≤ D ∧ ∀ i<d ∀ f∈C^i: ‖δf‖ ≥ ε·dist(f,B^i)

quote_A.text: there exist constants $D<\infty$, $\eps>0$, and finite connected pure $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes $X_m$, with $|X_m(0)|\longrightarrow\infty$

quote_B.text: Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of bounded-degree 𝔽2 coboundary expanders in every positive dimension.

notes: Gromov's question / CL2025 Problem 1.3 (a paper's problem, not a list → P2). The paper itself proves d≥3; the full all-dimension answer combines prior d=1,2 results, hence O1 with full_only_with_prior_results (O5 defensible for the d≥3 theorem alone).

quote_A.text: For all integers $m\ge n\ge3$ with $(m,n)\ne(3,3)$, \[ R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1. \]

quote_B.text: This establishes the cycle–clique conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp.

notes: Proof reduces to 3,099 finite instances checked by computer (proved inference rules). Keevash–Long–Skokan had already left only finitely many open pairs, but the proof does not rely on their constant.

claim_formal: ∃ countable division ring D, char 0, center F, x,y∈D: D=F[x,y] ∧ [D:F]=∞ ∧ ∀a∈D a algebraic over F

quote_A.text: There is a countable division ring $D$ of characteristic zero, with center $F=Z(D)$, and elements $x,y\in D$ such that \[ D=F[x,y]=F(x,y),\qquad [D:F]=\infty, \]

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the Kurosh problem for division rings.

notes: Kurosh's 1941 question (Problem (K)) treated as an open question (P2); some would label it P1. Counterexample to a universal question → M3 per tie-break 5.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive G with p_c(G)<1: P_{p_c}(∃ infinite open cluster)=0

quote_A.text: If $\pc(G)<1$, then \[ \PP_{\pc(G)}(\text{there is an infinite open cluster})=0. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the bond form of the criticality conjecture of Benjamini and Schramm.

notes: Prefix: ∀ graphs, then an almost-sure statement about the random configuration (ℙ per tie-break 4). M4 (no infinite cluster) vs M1. 'Bond form' only: if the conjecture is read as also covering site percolation, O5 would apply. Second manuscript: bond and site on ℤ^3 (own Lean comparator).

claim_formal: ∀ c∈(0,2]: the balanced-torus plane law P_c exists and h_δ → σ(c)Γ in law as δ→0, with σ(c)²=1/arcsin(c/2)

quote_A.text: As \(\delta\downarrow0\) through arbitrary positive real values, the fields \(h_\delta\) converge to \(\sigma(c)\Gamma\)

quote_B.text: The balanced square-lattice six-vertex height field with $`a=b=1`$ and $`0\lt c\le2`$ converges to a Gaussian free field, including at the endpoint c = 2.

notes: Posed problem is the Coulomb-gas/physics prediction of GFF convergence with this multiplier (Di Francesco–Saleur–Zuber); no named conjecture in the inputs, so P1 is low confidence. DKLM2026 had [√3,2]; this covers the full range and uses DKLM at c=2 and for amplitude (hence full_only_with_prior_results). O8 (extending DKLM's range) also defensible. Matrix: scaling limit with exact variance constant read as M9; M7 possible.

claim_formal: for uniform n-step SAW γ on the honeycomb lattice: ∀δ,k>0 ∃C,n₀ ∀n≥n₀: P_n(n^{3/4−δ} ≤ diam γ ≤ n^{3/4+δ}, local mass/covering exponents 4/3) ≥ 1−C n^{−k}

quote_A.text: n^{3/4-\delta}&\le D(\gamma)\le n^{3/4+\delta}

quote_B.text: Proves the diameter form of Nienhuis's predicted three-quarter exponent

notes: Nienhuis's ν=3/4 prediction is usually for 2D lattices generally and for end-to-end distance; here honeycomb lattice and diameter form with n^{o(1)} slack, hence O5 with restricted_range (O1 if the honeycomb diameter form is taken as the posed problem). 13 manuscripts give companion results: polygon tails, chord lengths R^{4/3}, cylinder exponents 1/6, nesting 1/12, bridge mass h^{-1/4}. Lean comparators cover intermediate results only (bridge sums finite, free energy, strip mass, bridge mass).

claim_formal: ∃ finitely generated residually finite group G: cd(G)=2 ∧ gd(G)=3

quote_A.text: There is a finitely generated residually finite group $G$ such that \[ \cdim G=2,\qquad \gdim G=3. \]

quote_B.text: disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

notes: Explicit witness: height kernel (Bestvina–Brady group) of a RAAG over a flag triangulation of an explicit acyclic presentation complex. Lean states it for that explicit group.

claim_formal: ∀ h>0: ℙ-a.s. the 2D Anderson operator H_v (v_x iid uniform on [−h,h]) has pure-point spectrum with σ(H_v)=[−4−h,4+h]

quote_A.text: For each fixed $h>0$, almost surely $H_v$ has pure-point spectral type, admits a complete orthonormal eigenbasis

quote_B.text: This resolves the pure-point assertion of the two-dimensional Anderson localization conjecture for the uniform single-site law.

notes: Family bundles two headlines: 2D pure point at every disorder (Simon Problem 2) and d≥3 purely a.c. spectrum on a fixed interval at weak disorder (Simon Problem 1, an existence-of-ac-spectrum claim, ∀∃ M2-like). Labelled the 2D result (first in summary, has Lean). O5 because only the uniform single-site law and pure-point part (not dynamical localization). Simon's list taken as an explicit numbered problem list (P3). Lean asserts only that the spectrum equals [−4−h,4+h], not pure-point type, hence 'different'.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥1 ∀ finite-energy n-mode states ρ_A,ρ_B ∀ η∈[0,1]: g^{-1}(S(ρ_C)/n) ≥ η g^{-1}(S(ρ_A)/n) + (1−η) g^{-1}(S(ρ_B)/n)

quote_A.text: g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_C)}n\right) \ge \eta\,g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_A)}n\right) +(1-\eta)\,g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{S(\rho_B)}n\right)

quote_B.text: This resolves the entropy photon-number conjecture in this finite-energy setting

notes: Finite-energy restriction is mild (O5 possible if the conjecture is read for all states). Corollaries: minimum output entropy of thermal attenuator tensor powers; capacity region of the degraded pure-loss bosonic broadcast channel.

claim_formal: ∃ finitely generated torsion-free group Γ: μ^r_Γ: K_0(BΓ)→K_0(C*_r Γ) has a kernel class of infinite order (rational injectivity of coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes fails)

quote_A.text: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group \(\Ginj\), an injective homomorphism \(i:\Z^2\to \Ginj\)

quote_B.text: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly.

notes: Family bundles three counterexamples: injectivity failure (labelled), surjectivity failure via a projection of irrational trace, and a torsion-free counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture. All are ∃/M3/P1/O2.

claim_formal: ∃ unital infinite-dimensional simple C*-algebra A with faithful tracial state: all nonzero irreducible representations of A are unitarily equivalent (so A ≇ K(H)), in ZFC

quote_A.text: There exists a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ with a faithful tracial state such that all its nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent.

quote_B.text: Tanaka gives another ZFC construction with a faithful tracial state \cite[Theorems~1.1, 4.1 and~5.3]{Tanaka2026}, so the existence conclusion of Theorem~\ref{na:main} is already present there.

notes: Naimark's problem answered negatively in ZFC; earlier counterexamples needed ◇ or other set-theoretic hypotheses. Tie-break 9 → O9 because the paper credits Tanaka's earlier ZFC construction.

claim_formal: K = K_3 = {0,2,3}: at p=3 the standard Kervaire classes b_j survive in the mod-3 ASS exactly for j∈{0,2,3} (stems 10, 106, 322), each with an order-3 representative

quote_A.text: At the prime three, \[ K=K_3=\{0,2,3\}. \]

quote_B.text: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three

notes: Complete determination of the surviving set → M6 (M9 defensible). Problem posed for all odd primes; settling p=3 → O5 with restricted_range per tie-break 6. Unstable corollaries: H-space splittings of Ω S^{2n+1}{3}, homotopy-associative T^{2n+1}(3) iff n∈{3,27,81}.

claim_formal: ∃ finite connected 3-dim CW complex X: H_i(X̃;ℤ)=0 (i>2) ∧ ∀M H^3(X;M)=0 ∧ X not ≃ any finite complex of dim ≤2

quote_A.text: There is a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex $X$ such that

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer to Wall's finite $`D(2)`$ problem.

notes: Wall's D(2) problem appears as Problem D3 in Wall's 1979 problem list (explicit numbered list → P3); summary calls it a conjecture (P1 alternative).

claim_formal: ∀ closed smooth Riemannian surface (M,g) ∃ C^∞ isometric immersion F:(M,g)→ℝ^4

quote_A.text: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface $(M,g)$ admits a $C^\infty$ isometric immersion into $(\R^4,\delta_4)$

quote_B.text: This resolves the closed-surface form of the classical four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem.

notes: Gromov's/Chern's question is for arbitrary smooth surfaces (compactness qualification uncertain); the closed case → O5 restricted_range. O1 if the closed-surface form is taken as the posed problem.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∀ smooth Riemannian metric g on S^n: ∃^∞ prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images

quote_A.text: there are infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise different images

quote_B.text: We resolve the sphere case of the closed-geodesic infinitude problem

notes: Infinitude problem posed for all closed manifolds; sphere case → O5. n=2 is classical (Bangert, Franks, Hingston). Corollaries for spherical space forms and all closed 3-manifolds (using Perelman, Rademacher–Taimanov).

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∃ L_n ∀ K ∀ noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space X ∀ n-regular p∈X ∃ open U∋p, V⊂ℝ^n, F:U→V homeo with L_n^{-1}d ≤ |F(x)−F(z)| ≤ L_n d

quote_A.text: there exist an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(p\), an open set \(V\subset\R^n\), and a homeomorphism \(F:U\to V\)

quote_B.text: We resolve the regular-point bi-Lipschitz conjecture in the noncollapsed setting.

notes: 'In the noncollapsed setting' may indicate a restriction of a broader conjecture (then O5); Cheeger–Colding's original question concerns noncollapsed limits. Summary says constant point-dependent, theorem says L_n depends only on n.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth bounded simply connected Ω⊂ℝ² ∀ 0≠u in first positive Neumann eigenspace ∀ x∈Ω: ∇u(x)≠0 (hence min_∂Ω u < u(x) < max_∂Ω u)

quote_A.text: For every $0\ne u\in\V$, \[ \grad u(x)\ne0\qquad(x\in\Omega). \]

quote_B.text: We prove the strict hot spots conjecture for smooth bounded simply connected planar domains.

notes: Burdzy's Conjecture 1.2(ii) concerns simply connected planar domains; the theorem assumes C^∞ boundary, so O5 restricted_range (O1 if smoothness is regarded as inessential). Strict form, multiplicity allowed. M1 vs M4 (no interior critical point).
